text:
incident-bot: [SEV-2] Elevated errors for runtime-tensor-pt across multi-GPU sharded jobs. 503s up from 1% to 16% in 5m. Top symptom: NCCL timeouts, communicator init failures, and a few container exits. alert_id=inc-2026-03-15-6789 links: https://grafana/redwood/d/srv/runtime-tensor-pt

kai: paging SRE rotation now. @jules_oncall @maria @devin please triage. Any deploys?

maria: no deploys in last 40m (checked deploy-bot). Pulling logs from affected pods. Initial surface-level looks like NCCL errors + a couple of CUDA OOMs during communicator setup.

devin: client side showing retries for sharded requests where work spans >1 node. Single-GPU variants look fine. Could be fabric instability or a collective-init race.

kai: immediate plan: 1) identify affected nodes 2) reduce customer impact by routing to non-sharded fallbacks 3) escalate infra if host-level issues. Carol, prepare customer comms.

carol: on it. Prepping targeted banner for impacted customers. Early list: AcmePay (~12% of their requests), LumenHealth (~5%), BetaRetail (~3%). Will open tickets and mark support priority-high.

maria: logs snippet from pod runtime-pt-7f6b:
```
[2026-03-15T21:06:58Z] worker ERROR: ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled system error
[2026-03-15T21:06:58Z] worker NCCL WARN: Allreduce timed out, aborting
[2026-03-15T21:06:58Z] runtime ContainerExit code=137 signal=9
[2026-03-15T21:06:59Z] worker RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating tensor of size 2.7GB during comm init
```
Multiple pods on node-gpu-22 and node-gpu-23 show the same sequence.

kai: @infra-bot run quick host checks (dmesg, IB counters, NIC rx/tx errors) for node-gpu-22/23.

infra-bot: quick diag: node-gpu-22 shows intermittent IB link flaps at ~21:06UTC, node-gpu-23 shows NVLink ECC corrected on GPU1 and a few PCIe rescans. Full diag saved: /infra/diag/1745006789-node-gpu-22-23.json

devin: that matches: fabric flaps + ECC events will break NCCL communicator creation. Two fast mitigations available: A) route traffic to non-sharded model variant (no cross-GPU collectives) B) set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on affected pods to force TCP fallback for NCCL and restart them. Routing is lower blast and instant.

jules_oncall: I'm taking lead on mitigation. Maria, can you update runtime routing to send sharded requests away from the impacted node-pool? If routing can't be granular, we'll failover customers to single-GPU model variants globally for impacted routes.

maria: routing API call I'm running: POST /v1/routing/override {"selector":"model:sharded-pt","policy":"fallback:single-gpu","reason":"nccl fabric instability node-gpu-22/23"} -> response 202. Starting traffic shift now.

kai: Carol, send interim message to support: "We are experiencing degraded performance for sharded models. We're routing affected traffic to single-GPU fallbacks which may increase latency/cost. No data exposure. Engineers are remediating fabric issues."

carol: done. Support ticket IDs: SUP-5123 (AcmePay), SUP-5124 (LumenHealth). Message includes mitigation and ETA estimate 30-45m.

infra-bot: per host logs, there are repeated IB port down/up events on node-gpu-22's mlx5_0 and NVLink corrected ECC on node-gpu-23. Recommending cordon+drain node-gpu-22 for immediate remediation and schedule physical check for node-gpu-23.

elaine_ops: I'll cordon node-gpu-22 and evict pods gracefully. Command: kubectl cordon node-gpu-22 && kubectl drain node-gpu-22 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60. Will monitor for impact.

devin: caution: draining will cause more communicator tears during evacuation for sharded pods. Because we already routed sharded traffic away, new scheduling should prefer single-gpu variants; still expect some restart churn.

maria: started draining node-gpu-22. Evictions show pods rescheduled to other healthy GPU nodes. Sharded pods were already deprioritized by routing so we avoided large-scale cross-GPU restarts.

kai: parallel mitigation: let's try NCCL_IB_DISABLE approach for any remaining cross-node sharded pods on node-gpu-23 if routing didn't cover them. Maria, can you patch the runtime daemonset for a canary set with NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 and restart a small subset?

maria: applying patch to canary set runtime-shard-canary: set env NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 and restart 3 pods on node-gpu-23. Restart results: 2/3 pods returned healthy and completed model init; logs show NCCL using TCP fallback and no communicator timeouts.

kai: good. Can we roll this to remaining affected pool if stable?

maria: I'll roll patch to affected pool with 2 pod parallelism to reduce disruption. Rolling now.

infra-bot: note: NCCL over TCP reduces throughput and increases latency; long-term fix is to replace failed IB port/cable or NVLink module on node-gpu-23. Hardware ticket INF-789 opened.

devin: customer impact summary: AcmePay saw 12% of their requests get 503s during the first 10m, latency increased ~400ms for single-gpu fallbacks. LumenHealth saw <5% errors. No requests appear to have failed with data leakage.

carol: support updated customers with mitigation note and internal workaround. They've accepted the temporary performance regression.

jules_oncall: incident severity remains Sev-2 while hardware ticket and node remediation are pending. Postmortem owner? Elaine, can you take postmortem?

elaine_ops: taking postmortem ownership. I'll document timeline, root cause hypothesis (fabric NIC flaps + NVLink ECC), mitigation steps, and long-term actions (cable replacement, improved IB monitoring, alter runtime to prefer TCP fallback earlier on fabric flaps). Postmortem ETA 72h.

kai: actions summary: 1) Traffic routed to single-gpu fallbacks (maria) 2) node-gpu-22 cordoned/drained (elaine_ops) 3) NCCL_IB_DISABLE canary then roll (maria) 4) Hardware ticket INF-789 for node-gpu-23 (infra) 5) Support notifications to affected customers (carol) 6) Postmortem (elaine_ops).

maria: monitoring: error rate back down to 0.8% for runtime-tensor-pt, latency settling at +320ms for fallback path. Keeping the routing override for 2h while infra completes physical checks.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] alert suppressed, error_rate returned to baseline. link: https://grafana/redwood/d/srv/runtime-tensor-pt

kai: thanks all. Keep this thread updated with hardware replacement ETA and postmortem link.

elaine_ops: noted. I'll file the postmortem and include suggested follow-ups: 1) add automated fabric-flap detector that triggers early NCCL TCP fallback, 2) add per-node NVLink ECC aggregation to alert earlier, 3) refine routing policy to failover by node-pool tag faster.

support-bot: Created customer follow-up tasks: CUS-FUP-1101 (AcmePay), CUS-FUP-1102 (LumenHealth).

kai: closing on-call handoff in 10m unless new regressions. Good job everyone.
